en: Scenario '{name}' defined before rules in knowledge base
Move the scenario after the rules.
Misplaced '{kw}' before an expectation. An expectation belongs to a scenario; write "{name} expects answers [...]" without the leading '{kw}'.
Remove the leading '{kw}' from this line.
Missing trailing dot for 'expects answers' in scenario
Add a dot at the end of the line.
Reserved word '{word}' in template: a template cannot contain '{word}'; the template is cut off at that point
Reword the template so it does not contain the reserved word.
Template contains the reserved word '{word}', which cuts it off. Section keywords (scenario, query, the knowledge base, the ontology, ...) cannot appear inside a template.
Reword the template so it does not use the reserved word.
A template with a synonym cannot have other additions (defines global, opposite, prepositional, unknown, undefined).
Split the synonym into its own template, or remove the other additions.
A prepositional template must have exactly two arguments (found {n})
Use exactly two *variables* in the template.
A prepositional template must start with an argument (its first token must be a *variable*)
Move the *variable* to the very beginning of the template.
Stray '*': outside the templates section, '*' is only valid as multiplication inside an arithmetic expression.
Remove the '*'.
Missing template for '{name}'
Undefined predicate '{functor}/{arity}'
add a rule defining the predicate, or add fact sentences for it in the relevant scenarios.
"... is a {phrase}" matches no declared template; it was read as a bare is-a statement with the constant type '{phrase}'. A template was probably intended.
Declare a template for this sentence, using *variables* for its arguments, instead of relying on the generic "is a" form.
Predicate '{functor}/{arity}' is declared 'undefined' (scenario element) but has a definition in the knowledge base
remove the fact or rule from the knowledge base, or remove the 'undefined'/'scenario element' annotation from the template.
This predicate is not tested by any query: '{functor}/{arity}'
add a query that exercises the predicate, and add expected answers using 'expects answers' in a scenario.
Rule without variables: {head} if {body}
move the concrete data into a scenario; rules should use variables.
Missing rules: the program contains only facts and no rules.
add rules that derive conclusions from the facts.
Too many facts: facts ({facts}) outnumber rules ({rules}) by more than 5:1.
add rules that derive conclusions from the facts.
Test failed for query '{query}' in scenario '{scenario}'.{newline}Expected: {expected}{newline}Actual: {actual}

Test failed for query '{query}' in scenario '{scenario}'.{newline}Expected: {expected}{newline}Actual: {actual}{newline}Expected Unknowns: {expected_unknowns}{newline}Actual Unknowns: {actual_unknowns}
Test error for query '{query}' in scenario '{scenario}': {error}
Test failed for query '{query}' in scenario '{scenario}'
check the logic of your rules or the facts in the scenario.
Template '{template}' redefines a similar system template and there are no rules for it
Either change the template slightly or add some rules
Fact '{text}' introduces a variable rather than naming an individual, so it holds for everything
use a proper name (e.g. 'fluffy') or 'any' for the individual; if you really mean 'every ...', write it as a rule.
Fact '{text}' in scenario '{scenario}' introduces a variable ('a/an/some ...') rather than naming an individual, so it holds for everything
name the individual (a proper name like 'fluffy', or 'the ...', which is a constant in a scenario); if you really mean 'every ...', write it as a rule in the knowledge base.
In '{literal}', the value '{arg}' is itself a template instance (a compound term) — it seems you want to use a meta-template here

if so, make sure to precede the meta variable by 'that' in the template; if the value should instead be atomic, declare explicit types (or mark the inner template as prepositional) so the phrase is not absorbed into the argument.
The first statement does not declare a known target language / A primeira frase não declara uma linguagem alvo conhecida. Defaulting to English.
Parsing failed. Check for malformed sections or characters.
